gaps.concept: A low-trauma fragility fracture can establish osteoporosis even when the DEXA T-score is above −2.5.
gaps.why_tested: An older adult fractures a hip after a standing-height fall despite a T-score outside the osteoporosis range.

gaps.concept: DEXA T-scores from −1.0 to −2.5 indicate osteopenia; Z-scores compare bone density with age-matched peers.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks whether reduced bone density meets the osteoporosis threshold or suggests an unusually low value for age.

gaps.concept: Glucocorticoids suppress osteoblast formation and promote osteoblast and osteocyte apoptosis. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK278968/)
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops vertebral fragility fractures after prolonged glucocorticoid therapy; the question asks for the cellular mechanism.

gaps.concept: Hypogonadism, hyperparathyroidism, and malabsorption are secondary causes of osteoporosis.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with unexpectedly early or severe osteoporosis has an endocrine disorder or chronic malabsorption.

gaps.concept: Osteoporosis shows thinned trabeculae and enlarged marrow spaces while remaining normally mineralized.
gaps.why_tested: A bone biopsy must distinguish loss of bone quantity from excess unmineralized osteoid.

gaps.concept: Bisphosphonates are first-line drugs for typical osteoporosis and symptomatic Paget disease.
gaps.why_tested: A treatment-choice question presents a postmenopausal fragility fracture or painful, active Paget disease.

gaps.concept: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates inhibit farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase, preventing osteoclast protein prenylation.
gaps.why_tested: A pharmacology stem asks for the intracellular target of alendronate or zoledronic acid.

gaps.concept: Denosumab can cause hypocalcemia; stopping it may trigger rebound vertebral fractures. [Source](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/125320s216lbl.pdf)
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops symptomatic hypocalcemia after treatment or multiple vertebral fractures after discontinuation.

gaps.concept: Romosozumab blocks osteocyte sclerostin, releasing Wnt-mediated osteoblast activity; it carries a myocardial infarction and stroke warning. [Source](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2019/761062Orig1s000Lbl.pdf)
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks how anti-sclerostin therapy forms bone or identifies its characteristic serious adverse effect.

gaps.concept: Raloxifene is estrogenic in bone but antiestrogenic in breast and uterus; it lowers breast-cancer risk and increases venous thrombosis risk. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279050/)
gaps.why_tested: A postmenopausal patient with osteoporosis and elevated breast-cancer risk is offered a SERM.

gaps.concept: Calcitonin directly inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption and can lower serum calcium.
gaps.why_tested: A drug-mechanism question asks how calcitonin affects osteoclasts and calcium.

gaps.concept: Continuous PTH exposure favors osteoclast-mediated resorption, whereas intermittent PTH-analog exposure favors bone formation.
gaps.why_tested: A stem contrasts hyperparathyroidism with intermittent teriparatide treatment.

gaps.concept: Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D is the best measure of vitamin D stores and is low in nutritional osteomalacia.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with suspected vitamin D deficiency needs the appropriate vitamin D metabolite identified.

gaps.concept: Secondary hyperparathyroidism in vitamin D deficiency can maintain serum calcium near normal while causing phosphate wasting.
gaps.why_tested: A patient has osteomalacia with low phosphate and elevated PTH but a near-normal calcium level.

gaps.concept: Adult osteomalacia commonly causes diffuse bone pain and proximal muscle weakness or waddling gait.
gaps.why_tested: A patient has difficulty rising from a chair alongside bone tenderness and abnormal mineralization labs.

gaps.concept: Osteomalacia biopsy shows broad seams of unmineralized osteoid. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279150/)
gaps.why_tested: A histology image must distinguish defective mineralization from osteoporosis.

gaps.concept: Rickets radiographs show widened growth plates with metaphyseal cupping and fraying.
gaps.why_tested: A child with bowed legs has an imaging question centered on the growth plate.

gaps.concept: Vitamin D deficiency can result from poor intake or sunlight, malabsorption, or enzyme-inducing antiepileptic drugs.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which exposure or condition explains new osteomalacia or rickets.

gaps.concept: Renal 1α-hydroxylase deficiency causes low calcitriol; vitamin D receptor resistance causes high calcitriol despite rickets.
gaps.why_tested: Two children with hereditary rickets are distinguished by their 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels.

gaps.concept: X-linked PHEX loss increases FGF23, causing renal phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemic rickets. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK83985/)
gaps.why_tested: A child has rickets, low phosphate, normal calcium, and a family history suggesting X-linked inheritance.

gaps.concept: Paget disease progresses from excessive osteoclastic resorption to disorganized osteoblastic formation of weak woven bone.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks why an enlarged, dense pagetic bone remains vulnerable to fracture.

gaps.concept: Paget imaging can show cotton-wool skull opacities, flame-shaped long-bone lysis, or a picture-frame vertebra. [Source](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK279033/)
gaps.why_tested: An older adult with elevated alkaline phosphatase has a characteristic skull, long-bone, or vertebral radiograph.

gaps.concept: Familial Paget disease can involve SQSTM1/p62 mutations that enhance osteoclast RANK–NF-κB signaling.
gaps.why_tested: A genetic-mechanism question describes relatives with focal, high-turnover bone disease.

gaps.concept: Osteopetrosis may cause marrow failure and cranial-nerve compression despite increased bone density; radiographs can show Erlenmeyer-flask deformity.
gaps.why_tested: A child has dense, fracture-prone bones with pancytopenia or visual impairment.

gaps.concept: CLCN7 or TCIRG1 defects can impair osteoclast acidification and cause osteopetrosis.
gaps.why_tested: A genetics stem asks for an osteoclast defect beyond carbonic anhydrase II deficiency.
